Source: A 65-year-old man presents to the emergency department with sudden-onset altered mental status.
His temperature is 98.0°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 150/90 mmHg, pulse is 115/min, and respirations are 17/min.
His wife noticed that he was confused, slurring his speech, and had notable weakness that caused him to drop his cup of coffee.
The patient is not able to follow any commands for further neurologic evaluation but does not appear to be moving his right upper extremity.
He has a past medical history of diabetes and atrial fibrillation and is currently taking warfarin.
